verdicts.claim: Automatic checkpointing runs when a COMMIT leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more, and when the last connection closes. PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=N
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size, or when the last database connection on a database file closes'; pragma.html: 'Setting the auto-checkpoint size to zero or a negative value turns auto-checkpointing off.'

verdicts.claim: The 1000-page default is a compile-time value, SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT. wal.html equates 1000 pages with about 4MB.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'The SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT compile-time option can be used to specify a different default' and 'about 1000 pages (and is thus about 4MB in size)'.

verdicts.claim: Every checkpoint takes an exclusive checkpoint lock. A second checkpoint that runs at the same time gets SQLITE_BUSY, and its busy handler is not called.
verdicts.evidence: wal_checkpoint_v2: 'All calls obtain an exclusive "checkpoint" lock ... SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.'

verdicts.claim: FULL waits until no writer is active and all readers use the latest snapshot, then copies every frame and syncs the database. While pending, it blocks new writers
verdicts.evidence: wal_checkpoint_v2 FULL: 'blocks ... until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot ... new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.'

verdicts.claim: TRUNCATE does what RESTART does, then truncates the -wal file to zero bytes on success. NOOP copies zero frames and only returns the counts.
verdicts.evidence: wal_checkpoint_v2: TRUNCATE 'also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return'; NOOP 'always checkpoints zero frames. The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned'.

verdicts.claim: journal_size_limit defaults to -1, which means no limit. Otherwise, each commit or WAL reset truncates a larger -wal file down to the limit.
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'The default journal size limit is -1 (no limit).' and 'set the journal_size_limit to zero' for minimum size.

verdicts.claim: A busy value of 1 in the first column of wal_checkpoint means a RESTART, FULL, or TRUNCATE was blocked. Litestream logs 'forcing truncate checkpoint'
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'will be 1 if a RESTART or FULL or TRUNCATE checkpoint was blocked from completing'; Litestream lists both 'wal restarted by passive checkpoint, skipping truncate checkpoint' and 'forcing truncate checkpoint'.

verdicts.claim: The WAL-reset bug affects SQLite 3.7.0 through 3.51.2 and is fixed in 3.51.3 (2026-03-13). Backports exist in 3.44.6 and 3.50.7.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'likely present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) ... Backports ... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7.' Release log: 'Fix the WAL-reset database corruption bug.'

verdicts.claim: Aggressive manual checkpointing raises exposure to the WAL-reset bug. Tailscale took manual control of checkpoints and checkpointed very aggressively
verdicts.evidence: Tailscale: 'why we were more likely to hit the bug than other SQLite users: we take manual control of the checkpointing process, and we checkpoint very aggressively.'

verdicts.claim: A PASSIVE checkpoint that hits SQLITE_BUSY can be skipped without stalling writers. Litestream logs 'passive checkpoint skipped' and carries on.
verdicts.evidence: Litestream: 'Non-blocking—returns SQLITE_BUSY if readers or writers are active, which Litestream handles gracefully by logging "passive checkpoint skipped" and continuing'.
